text:
acme-dev: Hey team — our users are intermittently getting a 403 on the OAuth callback after signing in with GitHub. Happens ~10% of attempts. Works on first try usually, then fails if they retry. No recent deploys from our side. Anyone seen this?

support-ella: Sorry for the trouble. Can you paste a sample callback URL (with keys redacted) and tell us if they're using any proxy / CDN in front of your app?

acme-dev: Sample (redacted): https://app.acme.example/auth/callback?code=abc123&state=eyJhbGciOiJI... (long)
We use Cloudflare Workers to rewrite hostnames and route traffic to internal cluster. Also using SameSite=None cookies for session.

support-ella: Thanks — that long state stands out. Two quick hypotheses: 1) state is getting truncated/altered by CF worker or by some proxy (could cause mismatch) 2) PKCE code_verifier mismatch (if you do PKCE) or registered redirect URI mismatch (trailing slash?). Are you using PKCE for GitHub?

acme-dev: We use PKCE (mobile + web flows). State is a JWT-ish object base64url encoded. Some errors in logs show: "state mismatch" from our /auth/callback handler. No code_verifier errors logged.

sally (eng-platform): Paging @bob (devops) and @jordan (eng-security) — this looks like a URL encoding/truncation issue we saw before with Cloudflare Workers dropping '+' and '=' if not forwarded correctly. Can you grab a raw request log showing the query string? Preferably tcpdump or raw nginx access log with full query, not just application-level.

acme-dev: Putting a raw access log now — cropping sensitive parts: 
```
1949504301 - - [15/Mar/2026:09:12:34 +0000] "GET /auth/callback?code=abc123&state=eyJhbG...aGVyZQ== HTTP/1.1" 200 512 "-" "Mozilla/5.0"
```
But sometimes we see the state truncated: ends with `eyJhbG...aGVy` (missing final `==`).

support-ella: That truncation is consistent with an encoding/character stripping issue. GitHub state is base64url, padding optional but many libs include '=' padding. If '=' is removed by some intermediary, base64 decode can fail and server will treat as mismatch.

bob (devops): On CF Workers we recently had a rule that normalized query strings for caching, which dropped trailing '=' in some rules. I'll check our worker script for `URLSearchParams` vs raw `request.url` forwarding. If worker reconstructs URL with `new URL()` and uses `searchParams.toString()` that can alter ordering and may drop empty params or re-encode.

jordan (eng-security): Also check SameSite cookie behavior: if your state is stored client-side in a cookie and that cookie isn't sent because of SameSite or cookie domain mismatch, that will appear as state mismatch even if callback has correct state. Do you persist state in cookie or server session?

acme-dev: We store state in a Secure SameSite=None cookie named `_acme_state` for web. But the mobile apps use in-memory state + pkce. The 403s are from web users only. Cookie present on initial redirect but not consistently on callback (we're seeing no cookie in some callback requests).

support-ella: Two parallel issues keep popping up: cookie not being sent (SameSite/secure/domain) and query param truncation. Both can cause state mismatch. Let's narrow: can you run a reproduction from behind CF worker with curl emulating the browser (include user-agent and cookie) and capture what arrives at origin?

acme-dev: Repro script I'm using: 
```
# emulate initial redirect
curl -v -L "https://app.acme.example/oauth/authorize?client_id=...&redirect_uri=https://app.acme.example/auth/callback&state=eyJhbGciOiJI...aGVyZQ==" \
  -H "User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0"
# simulate callback
curl -v "https://app.acme.example/auth/callback?code=abc123&state=eyJhbGciOiJI...aGVyZQ==" \
  -H "Cookie: _acme_state=eyJhbGciOiJI...aGVyZQ==" -H "User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0"
```
At the origin logs, state is sometimes arriving as `eyJhbGciOiJI...aGVy` (no padding) and cookie header is missing in ~12% of requests.

sally (eng-platform): Thanks — that matches a worker-side caching rule dropping cookies on cache hit and normalizing query strings. Bob, can you confirm if we recently turned on Cache API or altered worker script?

bob (devops): Confirmed: we enabled a worker optimization last week that uses `event.respondWith(caches.open(...).match(request))` then reconstructs response for performance. In some code paths we rebuild a new Request with `new Request(url.toString(), { method: request.method, headers: request.headers })`. There's a known issue: when URLSearchParams contains `=` or `%3D` in param values, some helper libraries call `searchParams.toString()` which percent-encodes `=` differently and may drop padding. Also if we use `request.headers` directly it includes cookie, but our cache match logic uses a cache key that ignores cookies and may return a cached response lacking Set-Cookie or proper Vary. I'll push a patch to keep original raw query and forward `request` instead of rebuilding.

oauth-bot: Ticket #SUP-2026 created for this thread. Priority: P2. Assignee: bob (devops). Links: internal/infra/worker-rules-2026.

jordan (eng-security): Small actionable checklist while devops fixes: 
- Switch state encoding to base64url without padding (or better: use base64url with no padding explicitly) to make tolerant to `=` stripping.
- Or persist state server-side (session store keyed by a short nonce) and send only a short nonce as state param. Short nonce avoids query param mangling.
- For PKCE: make sure your code_challenge uses S256 and code_verifier is stored server-side to compare after token exchange.

acme-dev: We can do short-term quick fix: change state to base64url with no padding and update JS encode. Long-term we'll move to server-side session keyed by nonce. We'll also ask devops to roll back worker change if needed.

bob (devops): Rolled back the worker query normalization at 09:45 UTC and pushed a patch that preserves raw request url and forwards original headers; added tests for `%3D` roundtrip. Monitoring now.

support-ella: After rollback any change in failure rate?

acme-dev: Re-tested with curl and from users — so far 24 hours with no 403s in the web login path (was ~10% previously). Cookie now consistently reaches origin. Thanks.

bob (devops): Deployed fix: https://deploy.redwood/infra/worker/2026-03-15 (rollforward). Added unit tests and a small integration test that replicates long state + cookie.

sally (eng-platform): Follow-ups: 1) acme team — please implement server-side nonce so you don't rely on large state payloads in query strings; 2) infra — add e2e test for query param fidelity across workers; 3) security — confirm PKCE flow logs consistent.

acme-dev: Will implement server-side nonce this week and message when done. Appreciate the quick triage.

support-ella: Marking thread resolved for now. If it resurfaces please reopen or ping #eng-platform. :thumbsup:
